usage: om [-h] [--version] <command> ...

om — self-host anything, privately and safely (Podman + Caddy)

Everyday:
  init        Initialize a workspace in the current directory
  add         Scaffold a service or project
  start       Start services (and the core if needed)
  stop        Stop services (core stays up)
  restart     Restart services
  status      Show core and workspace status
  logs        Show a service's logs
  doctor      Diagnose the installation and security perimeter

Services:
  edit        Edit a service's labels (scope, port, icon, ...)
  check       Check a compose file against om's rules (writes nothing)
  remove      Remove a service (moved to .om/trash)
  disable     Stop a service and keep it off (reversible with `om enable`)
  enable      Undo `om disable`
  shell       Open a shell (or run a command) in a service
  dev         Start a project and follow its logs
  update      Move pinned images to the newest digests, commit the lock, redeploy
  scripts     List workspace scripts
  run         Run a workspace script
  routes      Show this workspace's URLs
  preview     Run a branch as its own throw-away workspace: om preview <branch> | rm <branch> | list

Deploy and GitOps:
  sync        Pull from git, reconcile, health-check, roll back on failure
  autosync    Scheduled GitOps sync for this workspace
  drift       Compare the workspace with its git remote
  lock        Pin images missing from .om/lock.json to their registry digest
  log         Generations of this workspace (deploy history)
  rollback    Deploy an earlier generation's commit (default: the previous one)
  fsck        Verify generation chain, signature, and running images against the lock
  secrets     Service secrets (age): init, set <project>/<name>, list, rekey; decrypt / migrate <file> <project>/<name> read and move old om-v2 files
  policy      Check compose files against the policy gate

Network and security:
  exposure    Who can reach what: this machine, the VPN's devices, the LAN; per service, its address rules and outbound access
  vpn         VPNs whose devices reach the private tier: list, trust|untrust <iface>, allow|disallow <device>, devices
  firewall    Host firewall: only om's ingress reachable; `log`: who was refused, who connected
  auth        Require a login for the private tier
  links       Cross-workspace links (om.link / om.link.allow)
  network     Show this workspace's network, or harden it (internal)
  egress      Show refused outbound calls and the om.egress line to allow them
  ports       Show host port bindings and any leaks

Platform and upkeep:
  core        Manage the Global Core (edge, router, dashboard)
  config      Settings in om.env: show, get <KEY>, set KEY=value (checked, file kept 0600), unset <KEY>
  boot        Start containers automatically at boot
  notify      Notifications about image updates: `om notify test` sends one on every channel
  list        List registered workspaces
  prune       List images nothing uses and no lock pins; --yes removes them
  scan        Count critical/high vulnerabilities in the pinned images (needs trivy or grype)
  reload      Regenerate routes and hot-reload the proxy
  down        Stop the workspace and the Global Core
  docs        List om's docs, or read one (om docs guide | architecture | design)
  completion  Print a shell completion script
  version     Print the version
  uninstall   Stop om and remove its command

Options:
  -h, --help  show this help
  --version   print the version

New here? Run `om docs start`, or `om` inside a folder to see where things stand.
Details of one command: om <command> --help
